security_audit.summary: Two CDN script examples load executable third-party code without integrity protection, so they are confirmed low-severity supply-chain risks. The documented npx validation commands are a separate medium-severity package-execution risk when the CLI is absent. The remaining static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code delimiters, CSS or JavaScript syntax, benign local checks, and ordinary documentation terms.

remediation.issue: Remote GSAP scripts lack integrity protection.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle or self-host the reviewed GSAP dependency. If a CDN is required, pin the version and add a verified SRI integrity attribute with crossorigin.

remediation.issue: npx commands can download and execute a package.
remediation.suggestion: Require an installed, version-pinned hyperframes CLI or use npx with an explicit reviewed version. Tell users to verify the package source before execution.

content.value_statement: Video composition work can fail when timing, media, and layout rules conflict. This skill provides a clear HTML contract for building and validating predictable HyperFrames projects.
actual_capabilities: Defines standalone and modular composition structures.
Explains timing with data attributes, clips, and track indexes.
Guides sub-composition IDs, templates, and timeline registration.
Documents framework-owned video and audio placement rules.
Provides deterministic rendering and layout guidance.
Lists validation steps for checks, snapshots, previews, and approved renders.
limitations: It documents the HyperFrames composition contract and does not render video itself.
It does not provide creative direction, narration, or media assets.
It assumes access to a compatible HyperFrames runtime and CLI.
External CDN and npx examples require dependency review before use.

use_cases.title: Create a first composition
use_cases.description: Start a small HTML video composition with a sized root, clips, and one paused timeline.

use_cases.title: Organize a multi-scene video
use_cases.description: Split a multi-scene project into sub-compositions with consistent IDs and track timing.

use_cases.title: Review an existing project
use_cases.description: Check media placement, deterministic animation, and validation steps before a render.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal HyperFrames composition for a 10-second product title card. Explain each required timing attribute.

prompt_templates.title: Add a timed scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a new six-second clip to my existing HyperFrames composition. Preserve current IDs, tracks, and media paths.

prompt_templates.title: Build modular scenes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a modular HyperFrames project with three sequential scenes and continuous root audio. Include the required sub-composition wiring.

prompt_templates.title: Audit rendering readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HyperFrames project against the composition contract. Identify deterministic rendering, layout, media, and timeline issues before rendering.

output_examples.input: Create a 15-second product introduction with two scenes.
output: A standalone or modular structure recommendation.
Timed scene boundaries and track assignments.
A checklist for timeline, media, and layout requirements.

output_examples.input: Review a composition that contains a video inside a sub-composition.
output: The video must move to a direct child of the host root.
The scene template should retain only its visual frame and overlays.
Host timeline timing must use the scene start plus local offset.

best_practices: Read the relevant reference before changing composition structure or media.
Use one paused timeline per composition and keep timeline keys equal to composition IDs.
Run checks and inspect snapshots before requesting an approved render.
anti_patterns: Do not put video or audio inside a sub-composition template.
Do not use clocks, unseeded randomness, network input, or infinite repeats during rendering.
Do not change unrelated timing, IDs, variables, or media paths in an existing project.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create deterministic HyperFrames video compositions from HTML.

faq.question: When should I use a modular project?
faq.answer: Use modular structure when a video has clear scene cuts, reusable scenes, or large scene markup.

faq.question: Can a sub-composition contain video or audio?
faq.answer: No. Video and audio must be direct children of the host root.

faq.question: Why must the timeline be paused?
faq.answer: A paused timeline lets the renderer seek to each exact frame deterministically.

faq.question: Does this skill create media assets?
faq.answer: No. It defines composition structure and media placement, not asset creation.

faq.question: When should I render the project?
faq.answer: Render only after checks pass, snapshots are reviewed, and the user approves the output.
